domain: androidworld
task_id: SimpleSmsSendClipboardContent
native:
  user_goal:
    text: Send an SMS in Simple SMS Messenger to the task's target number, using the clipboard content as the message body.
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/single/sms.py::SimpleSmsSendClipboardContent
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/single/sms.py::SimpleSmsSendClipboardContent.initialize_task
  benchmark_success:
    text: 'Native success requires `done=true` and an evaluator pass: a sent-SMS row within 5 minutes matches the task number and expected clipboard text under the evaluator''s fuzzy-match rule, the foreground package is `com.simplemobiletools.smsmessenger`, and final UI evidence does not show a `Sending` stall.'
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/suite_utils.py::_run_task
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::SimpleSMSSendSms.is_successful
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::was_sent
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::_check_if_stuck_at_sending
    - official/install/android_world/utils/fuzzy_match_lib.py::fuzzy_match
  checked_by:
    text: AndroidWorld runner `_run_task` done gate plus `SimpleSMSSendSms.is_successful`.
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/suite_utils.py::_run_task
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::SimpleSMSSendSms.is_successful
  decisive_artifacts:
  - artifact: Retained task-instance inputs / clipboard-initialization record
    question: 'What were the evaluator inputs: target `number` and expected clipboard text `message` that initialization placed on the clipboard?'
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::SimpleSMSSendSms.schema
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/single/sms.py::SimpleSmsSendClipboardContent.initialize_task
  - artifact: Retained episode end status or trace
    question: Did the episode end with `done=true`?
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/suite_utils.py::_run_task
  - artifact: Retained sent-SMS query output or equivalent telephony snapshot at evaluation time
    question: Is there a `content://sms/sent` row whose normalized address matches the task number, whose body fuzzy-matches the expected clipboard text, and whose timestamp is within 5 minutes of evaluator time?
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::SimpleSMSSendSms.get_sent_messages
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::was_sent
    - official/install/android_world/utils/fuzzy_match_lib.py::fuzzy_match
  - artifact: Retained final evaluator observation
    question: At evaluation time, was the foreground package `com.simplemobiletools.smsmessenger`, and did final UI evidence avoid any text starting with `Sending`?
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::SimpleSMSSendSms.is_successful
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::_check_if_stuck_at_sending
  success_if:
  - text: Episode-end evidence shows `done=true`; task-input evidence gives the target number and expected clipboard text; sent-SMS evidence shows a qualifying recent row matching both under the evaluator's normalization/fuzzy rule; final foreground evidence shows `com.simplemobiletools.smsmessenger`; and final UI evidence shows no text starting with `Sending`.
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/suite_utils.py::_run_task
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::SimpleSMSSendSms.is_successful
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::was_sent
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/single/sms.py::SimpleSmsSendClipboardContent.initialize_task
    - official/install/android_world/utils/fuzzy_match_lib.py::fuzzy_match
  fail_if:
  - text: Episode-end evidence shows `done=false`.
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/suite_utils.py::_run_task
  - text: Episode-end evidence shows `done=true`, task-input evidence gives the target number and expected clipboard text, and sent-SMS evidence rules out any qualifying recent row matching both under the evaluator's normalization/fuzzy rule.
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/suite_utils.py::_run_task
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::SimpleSMSSendSms.is_successful
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::was_sent
    - official/install/android_world/utils/fuzzy_match_lib.py::fuzzy_match
  - text: Episode-end evidence shows `done=true`, and final foreground evidence shows the evaluator-time package was not `com.simplemobiletools.smsmessenger`.
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/suite_utils.py::_run_task
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::SimpleSMSSendSms.is_successful
  undecided_if:
  - text: 'The retained record does not let a reviewer reconstruct one or more native checks: task inputs (`number` and expected clipboard text `message`), episode `done`, sent-SMS rows/timestamps, or the final foreground/UI observation.'
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::SimpleSMSSendSms.schema
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/single/sms.py::SimpleSmsSendClipboardContent.initialize_task
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::SimpleSMSSendSms.is_successful
    - official/install/android_world/suite_utils.py::_run_task
  - text: Final UI evidence shows text starting with `Sending`, or other retained exception evidence indicates the evaluator would raise, and the remaining artifacts do not independently establish success or failure.
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::_check_if_stuck_at_sending
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sms_validators.py::SimpleSMSSendSms.is_successful
    - official/install/android_world/suite_utils.py::_run_task
    rationale: The released runner records evaluator exceptions separately rather than as a native counted success or failure.
stronger:
  additional_conditions:
  - id: exact_clipboard_body
    text: Beyond native success, the sent SMS body exactly equals the task's clipboard text `message`, not merely a fuzzy match.
    rationale: The user goal is to send the clipboard content itself, while the native validator accepts approximate body matches through `fuzzy_match`.

    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/single/sms.py::SimpleSmsSendClipboardContent.initialize_task

  - id: send_via_simple_sms_ui
    text: Beyond native success, retained trace evidence shows the message was actually composed and sent from Simple SMS Messenger, not sent elsewhere and followed by ending in that app.

    decisive_artifacts:
    - artifact: Retained foreground/action trace plus sent-SMS evidence
      question: Does the retained trace show compose-and-send actions occurring while Simple SMS Messenger was foregrounded?
      support:
      - official/install/android_world/task_evals/single/sms.py::SimpleSmsSendClipboardContent

- Usually there will be multiple ways to complete a task, pick the easiest one. Also when something does not work as expected (due to various reasons), sometimes a simple retry can solve the problem, but if it doesn't (you can see that from the history), try to switch to other solutions.

Here are some useful guidelines you need to follow:
General
- Usually there will be multiple ways to complete a task, pick the easiest one. Also when something does not work as expected (due to various reasons), sometimes a simple retry can solve the problem, but if it doesn't (you can see that from the history), try to switch to other solutions.
- Sometimes you may need to navigate the phone to gather information needed to complete the task, for example if user asks "what is my schedule tomorrow", then you may want to open the calendar app (using the `open_app` action), look up information there, answer user's question (using the `answer` action) and finish (using the `status` action with complete as goal_status).
- For requests that are questions (or chat messages), remember to use the `answer` action to reply to user explicitly before finish! Merely displaying the answer on the screen is NOT sufficient (unless the goal is something like "show me ...").
- If the desired state is already achieved (e.g., enabling Wi-Fi when it's already on), you can just complete the task.
Action Related
- Use the `open_app` action whenever you want to open an app (nothing will happen if the app is not installed), do not use the app drawer to open an app unless all other ways have failed.
- Use the `input_text` action whenever you want to type something (including password) instead of clicking characters on the keyboard one by one. Sometimes there is some default text in the text field you want to type in, remember to delete them before typing.
- For `click`, `long_press` and `input_text`, the index parameter you pick must be VISIBLE in the screenshot and also in the UI element list given to you (some elements in the list may NOT be visible on the screen so you can not interact with them).
- Consider exploring the screen by using the `scroll` action with different directions to reveal additional content.
- The direction parameter for the `scroll` action can be confusing sometimes as it's opposite to swipe, for example, to view content at the bottom, the `scroll` direction should be set to "down". It has been observed that you have difficulties in choosing the correct direction, so if one does not work, try the opposite as well.
Text Related Operations
- Normally to select some text on the screen: <i> Enter text selection mode by long pressing the area where the text is, then some of the words near the long press point will be selected (highlighted with two pointers indicating the range) and usually a text selection bar will also appear with options like `copy`, `paste`, `select all`, etc. <ii> Select the exact text you need. Usually the text selected from the previous step is NOT the one you want, you need to adjust the range by dragging the two pointers. If you want to select all text in the text field, simply click the `select all` button in the bar.
- At this point, you don't have the ability to drag something around the screen, so in general you can not select arbitrary text.
- To delete some text: the most traditional way is to place the cursor at the right place and use the backspace button in the keyboard to delete the characters one by one (can long press the backspace to accelerate if there are many to delete). Another approach is to first select the text you want to delete, then click the backspace button in the keyboard.
- To copy some text: first select the exact text you want to copy, which usually also brings up the text selection bar, then click the `copy` button in bar.
- To paste text into a text box, first long press the text box, then usually the text selection bar will appear with a `paste` button in it.
- When typing into a text field, sometimes an auto-complete dropdown list will appear. This usually indicating this is a enum field and you should try to select the best match by clicking the corresponding one in the list.

General
- Usually there will be multiple ways to complete a task, pick the easiest one. Also when something does not work as expected (due to various reasons), sometimes a simple retry can solve the problem, but if it doesn't (you can see that from the history), try to switch to other solutions.

- For requests that are questions (or chat messages), remember to use the `answer` action to reply to user explicitly before finish! Merely displaying the answer on the screen is NOT sufficient (unless the goal is something like "show me ...").
- If the desired state is already achieved (e.g., enabling Wi-Fi when it's already on), you can just complete the task.
Action Related

- Consider exploring the screen by using the `scroll` action with different directions to reveal additional content.

Usually the text selected from the previous step is NOT the one you want, you need to adjust the range by dragging the two pointers. If you want to select all text in the text field, simply click the `select all` button in the bar.

Another approach is to first select the text you want to delete, then click the backspace button in the keyboard.
- To copy some text: first select the exact text you want to copy, which usually also brings up the text selection bar, then click the `copy` button in bar.
- To paste text into a text box, first long press the text box, then usually the text selection bar will appear with a `paste` button in it.

General

General
- Usually there will be multiple ways to complete a task, pick the easiest one. Also when something does not work as expected (due to various reasons), sometimes a simple retry can solve the problem, but if it doesn't (you can see that from the history), try to switch to other solutions.
- Sometimes you may need to navigate the phone to gather information needed to complete the task, for example if user asks "what is my schedule tomorrow", then you may want to open the calendar app (using the `open_app` action), look up information there, answer user's question (using the `answer` action) and finish (using the `status` action with complete as goal_status).
- For requests that are questions (or chat messages), remember to use the `answer` action to reply to user explicitly before finish! Merely displaying the answer on the screen is NOT sufficient (unless the goal is something like "show me ...").
- If the desired state is already achieved (e.g., enabling Wi-Fi when it's already on), you can just complete the task.
Action Related
- Use the `open_app` action whenever you want to open an app (nothing will happen if the app is not installed), do not use the app drawer to open an app unless all other ways have failed.
- Use the `input_text` action whenever you want to type something (including password) instead of clicking characters on the keyboard one by one. Sometimes there is some default text in the text field you want to type in, remember to delete them before typing.

- Consider exploring the screen by using the `scroll` action with different directions to reveal additional content.

Usually the text selected from the previous step is NOT the one you want, you need to adjust the range by dragging the two pointers. If you want to select all text in the text field, simply click the `select all` button in the bar.

Another approach is to first select the text you want to delete, then click the backspace button in the keyboard.
- To copy some text: first select the exact text you want to copy, which usually also brings up the text selection bar, then click the `copy` button in bar.
- To paste text into a text box, first long press the text box, then usually the text selection bar will appear with a `paste` button in it.

General

General
- Usually there will be multiple ways to complete a task, pick the easiest one. Also when something does not work as expected (due to various reasons), sometimes a simple retry can solve the problem, but if it doesn't (you can see that from the history), try to switch to other solutions.
- Sometimes you may need to navigate the phone to gather information needed to complete the task, for example if user asks "what is my schedule tomorrow", then you may want to open the calendar app (using the `open_app` action), look up information there, answer user's question (using the `answer` action) and finish (using the `status` action with complete as goal_status).
- For requests that are questions (or chat messages), remember to use the `answer` action to reply to user explicitly before finish! Merely displaying the answer on the screen is NOT sufficient (unless the goal is something like "show me ...").
- If the desired state is already achieved (e.g., enabling Wi-Fi when it's already on), you can just complete the task.
Action Related
- Use the `open_app` action whenever you want to open an app (nothing will happen if the app is not installed), do not use the app drawer to open an app unless all other ways have failed.
- Use the `input_text` action whenever you want to type something (including password) instead of clicking characters on the keyboard one by one. Sometimes there is some default text in the text field you want to type in, remember to delete them before typing.

- Consider exploring the screen by using the `scroll` action with different directions to reveal additional content.

Text Related Operations

Usually the text selected from the previous step is NOT the one you want, you need to adjust the range by dragging the two pointers. If you want to select all text in the text field, simply click the `select all` button in the bar.

Another approach is to first select the text you want to delete, then click the backspace button in the keyboard.
- To copy some text: first select the exact text you want to copy, which usually also brings up the text selection bar, then click the `copy` button in bar.
- To paste text into a text box, first long press the text box, then usually the text selection bar will appear with a `paste` button in it.

General
- Usually there will be multiple ways to complete a task, pick the easiest one. Also when something does not work as expected (due to various reasons), sometimes a simple retry can solve the problem, but if it doesn't (you can see that from the history), try to switch to other solutions.
- Sometimes you may need to navigate the phone to gather information needed to complete the task, for example if user asks "what is my schedule tomorrow", then you may want to open the calendar app (using the `open_app` action), look up information there, answer user's question (using the `answer` action) and finish (using the `status` action with complete as goal_status).
- For requests that are questions (or chat messages), remember to use the `answer` action to reply to user explicitly before finish! Merely displaying the answer on the screen is NOT sufficient (unless the goal is something like "show me ...").
- If the desired state is already achieved (e.g., enabling Wi-Fi when it's already on), you can just complete the task.

- Use the `open_app` action whenever you want to open an app (nothing will happen if the app is not installed), do not use the app drawer to open an app unless all other ways have failed.

Another approach is to first select the text you want to delete, then click the backspace button in the keyboard.

General
- Usually there will be multiple ways to complete a task, pick the easiest one. Also when something does not work as expected (due to various reasons), sometimes a simple retry can solve the problem, but if it doesn't (you can see that from the history), try to switch to other solutions.

- For requests that are questions (or chat messages), remember to use the `answer` action to reply to user explicitly before finish! Merely displaying the answer on the screen is NOT sufficient (unless the goal is something like "show me ...").
- If the desired state is already achieved (e.g., enabling Wi-Fi when it's already on), you can just complete the task.
Action Related

- Consider exploring the screen by using the `scroll` action with different directions to reveal additional content.

Usually the text selected from the previous step is NOT the one you want, you need to adjust the range by dragging the two pointers. Another approach is to first select the text you want to delete, then click the backspace button in the keyboard.

General
- Usually there will be multiple ways to complete a task, pick the easiest one. Also when something does not work as expected (due to various reasons), sometimes a simple retry can solve the problem, but if it doesn't (you can see that from the history), try to switch to other solutions.

- For requests that are questions (or chat messages), remember to use the `answer` action to reply to user explicitly before finish! Merely displaying the answer on the screen is NOT sufficient (unless the goal is something like "show me ...").
- If the desired state is already achieved (e.g., enabling Wi-Fi when it's already on), you can just complete the task.
Action Related

- Consider exploring the screen by using the `scroll` action with different directions to reveal additional content.

Text Related Operations

Usually the text selected from the previous step is NOT the one you want, you need to adjust the range by dragging the two pointers. If you want to select all text in the text field, simply click the `select all` button in the bar.

Another approach is to first select the text you want to delete, then click the backspace button in the keyboard.
- To copy some text: first select the exact text you want to copy, which usually also brings up the text selection bar, then click the `copy` button in bar.
- To paste text into a text box, first long press the text box, then usually the text selection bar will appear with a `paste` button in it.

General
- Usually there will be multiple ways to complete a task, pick the easiest one. Also when something does not work as expected (due to various reasons), sometimes a simple retry can solve the problem, but if it doesn't (you can see that from the history), try to switch to other solutions.

- For requests that are questions (or chat messages), remember to use the `answer` action to reply to user explicitly before finish! Merely displaying the answer on the screen is NOT sufficient (unless the goal is something like "show me ...").

Another approach is to first select the text you want to delete, then click the backspace button in the keyboard.

Here are some useful guidelines you need to follow:
General
- Usually there will be multiple ways to complete a task, pick the easiest one. Also when something does not work as expected (due to various reasons), sometimes a simple retry can solve the problem, but if it doesn't (you can see that from the history), try to switch to other solutions.
- Sometimes you may need to navigate the phone to gather information needed to complete the task, for example if user asks "what is my schedule tomorrow", then you may want to open the calendar app (using the `open_app` action), look up information there, answer user's question (using the `answer` action) and finish (using the `status` action with complete as goal_status).
- For requests that are questions (or chat messages), remember to use the `answer` action to reply to user explicitly before finish! Merely displaying the answer on the screen is NOT sufficient (unless the goal is something like "show me ...").
- If the desired state is already achieved (e.g., enabling Wi-Fi when it's already on), you can just complete the task.
Action Related
- Use the `open_app` action whenever you want to open an app (nothing will happen if the app is not installed), do not use the app drawer to open an app unless all other ways have failed.
- Use the `input_text` action whenever you want to type something (including password) instead of clicking characters on the keyboard one by one. Sometimes there is some default text in the text field you want to type in, remember to delete them before typing.
- For `click`, `long_press` and `input_text`, the index parameter you pick must be VISIBLE in the screenshot and also in the UI element list given to you (some elements in the list may NOT be visible on the screen so you can not interact with them).
- Consider exploring the screen by using the `scroll` action with different directions to reveal additional content.
- The direction parameter for the `scroll` action can be confusing sometimes as it's opposite to swipe, for example, to view content at the bottom, the `scroll` direction should be set to "down". - For requests that are questions (or chat messages), remember to use the `answer` action to reply to user explicitly before finish! Merely displaying the answer on the screen is NOT sufficient (unless the goal is something like "show me ...").

Here are some useful guidelines you need to follow:
General
- Usually there will be multiple ways to complete a task, pick the easiest one. Also when something does not work as expected (due to various reasons), sometimes a simple retry can solve the problem, but if it doesn't (you can see that from the history), try to switch to other solutions.
- Sometimes you may need to navigate the phone to gather information needed to complete the task, for example if user asks "what is my schedule tomorrow", then you may want to open the calendar app (using the `open_app` action), look up information there, answer user's question (using the `answer` action) and finish (using the `status` action with complete as goal_status).
- For requests that are questions (or chat messages), remember to use the `answer` action to reply to user explicitly before finish! Merely displaying the answer on the screen is NOT sufficient (unless the goal is something like "show me ...").
- If the desired state is already achieved (e.g., enabling Wi-Fi when it's already on), you can just complete the task.
Action Related
- Use the `open_app` action whenever you want to open an app (nothing will happen if the app is not installed), do not use the app drawer to open an app unless all other ways have failed.
- Use the `input_text` action whenever you want to type something (including password) instead of clicking characters on the keyboard one by one. Sometimes there is some default text in the text field you want to type in, remember to delete them before typing.
- For `click`, `long_press` and `input_text`, the index parameter you pick must be VISIBLE in the screenshot and also in the UI element list given to you (some elements in the list may NOT be visible on the screen so you can not interact with them).
- Consider exploring the screen by using the `scroll` action with different directions to reveal additional content.
- The direction parameter for the `scroll` action can be confusing sometimes as it's opposite to swipe, for example, to view content at the bottom, the `scroll` direction should be set to "down". Here are some useful guidelines you need to follow:
General
- Usually there will be multiple ways to complete a task, pick the easiest one. Also when something does not work as expected (due to various reasons), sometimes a simple retry can solve the problem, but if it doesn't (you can see that from the history), try to switch to other solutions.
- Sometimes you may need to navigate the phone to gather information needed to complete the task, for example if user asks "what is my schedule tomorrow", then you may want to open the calendar app (using the `open_app` action), look up information there, answer user's question (using the `answer` action) and finish (using the `status` action with complete as goal_status).
- For requests that are questions (or chat messages), remember to use the `answer` action to reply to user explicitly before finish! Merely displaying the answer on the screen is NOT sufficient (unless the goal is something like "show me ...").
- If the desired state is already achieved (e.g., enabling Wi-Fi when it's already on), you can just complete the task.
Action Related
- Use the `open_app` action whenever you want to open an app (nothing will happen if the app is not installed), do not use the app drawer to open an app unless all other ways have failed.
- Use the `input_text` action whenever you want to type something (including password) instead of clicking characters on the keyboard one by one. Sometimes there is some default text in the text field you want to type in, remember to delete them before typing.
- For `click`, `long_press` and `input_text`, the index parameter you pick must be VISIBLE in the screenshot and also in the UI element list given to you (some elements in the list may NOT be visible on the screen so you can not interact with them).
- Consider exploring the screen by using the `scroll` action with different directions to reveal additional content.
- The direction parameter for the `scroll` action can be confusing sometimes as it's opposite to swipe, for example, to view content at the bottom, the `scroll` direction should be set to "down". Here are some useful guidelines you need to follow:
General
- Usually there will be multiple ways to complete a task, pick the easiest one. Also when something does not work as expected (due to various reasons), sometimes a simple retry can solve the problem, but if it doesn't (you can see that from the history), try to switch to other solutions.
- Sometimes you may need to navigate the phone to gather information needed to complete the task, for example if user asks "what is my schedule tomorrow", then you may want to open the calendar app (using the `open_app` action), look up information there, answer user's question (using the `answer` action) and finish (using the `status` action with complete as goal_status).
- For requests that are questions (or chat messages), remember to use the `answer` action to reply to user explicitly before finish! Merely displaying the answer on the screen is NOT sufficient (unless the goal is something like "show me ...").
- If the desired state is already achieved (e.g., enabling Wi-Fi when it's already on), you can just complete the task.

Here are some useful guidelines you need to follow:
General
- Usually there will be multiple ways to complete a task, pick the easiest one. Also when something does not work as expected (due to various reasons), sometimes a simple retry can solve the problem, but if it doesn't (you can see that from the history), try to switch to other solutions.
- Sometimes you may need to navigate the phone to gather information needed to complete the task, for example if user asks "what is my schedule tomorrow", then you may want to open the calendar app (using the `open_app` action), look up information there, answer user's question (using the `answer` action) and finish (using the `status` action with complete as goal_status).
- For requests that are questions (or chat messages), remember to use the `answer` action to reply to user explicitly before finish! Merely displaying the answer on the screen is NOT sufficient (unless the goal is something like "show me ...").
- If the desired state is already achieved (e.g., enabling Wi-Fi when it's already on), you can just complete the task.
Action Related
- Use the `open_app` action whenever you want to open an app (nothing will happen if the app is not installed), do not use the app drawer to open an app unless all other ways have failed.

Here are some useful guidelines you need to follow:
General
- Usually there will be multiple ways to complete a task, pick the easiest one. Also when something does not work as expected (due to various reasons), sometimes a simple retry can solve the problem, but if it doesn't (you can see that from the history), try to switch to other solutions.
- Sometimes you may need to navigate the phone to gather information needed to complete the task, for example if user asks "what is my schedule tomorrow", then you may want to open the calendar app (using the `open_app` action), look up information there, answer user's question (using the `answer` action) and finish (using the `status` action with complete as goal_status).
- For requests that are questions (or chat messages), remember to use the `answer` action to reply to user explicitly before finish! Merely displaying the answer on the screen is NOT sufficient (unless the goal is something like "show me ...").
- If the desired state is already achieved (e.g., enabling Wi-Fi when it's already on), you can just complete the task.
Action Related
- Use the `open_app` action whenever you want to open an app (nothing will happen if the app is not installed), do not use the app drawer to open an app unless all other ways have failed.
- Use the `input_text` action whenever you want to type something (including password) instead of clicking characters on the keyboard one by one. Sometimes there is some default text in the text field you want to type in, remember to delete them before typing.
- For `click`, `long_press` and `input_text`, the index parameter you pick must be VISIBLE in the screenshot and also in the UI element list given to you (some elements in the list may NOT be visible on the screen so you can not interact with them).
- Consider exploring the screen by using the `scroll` action with different directions to reveal additional content.
- The direction parameter for the `scroll` action can be confusing sometimes as it's opposite to swipe, for example, to view content at the bottom, the `scroll` direction should be set to "down". Here are some useful guidelines you need to follow:
General
- Usually there will be multiple ways to complete a task, pick the easiest one. Also when something does not work as expected (due to various reasons), sometimes a simple retry can solve the problem, but if it doesn't (you can see that from the history), try to switch to other solutions.
- Sometimes you may need to navigate the phone to gather information needed to complete the task, for example if user asks "what is my schedule tomorrow", then you may want to open the calendar app (using the `open_app` action), look up information there, answer user's question (using the `answer` action) and finish (using the `status` action with complete as goal_status).
- For requests that are questions (or chat messages), remember to use the `answer` action to reply to user explicitly before finish! Merely displaying the answer on the screen is NOT sufficient (unless the goal is something like "show me ...").
- If the desired state is already achieved (e.g., enabling Wi-Fi when it's already on), you can just complete the task.
Action Related
- Use the `open_app` action whenever you want to open an app (nothing will happen if the app is not installed), do not use the app drawer to open an app unless all other ways have failed.
- Use the `input_text` action whenever you want to type something (including password) instead of clicking characters on the keyboard one by one. Sometimes there is some default text in the text field you want to type in, remember to delete them before typing.
- For `click`, `long_press` and `input_text`, the index parameter you pick must be VISIBLE in the screenshot and also in the UI element list given to you (some elements in the list may NOT be visible on the screen so you can not interact with them).
- Consider exploring the screen by using the `scroll` action with different directions to reveal additional content.
- The direction parameter for the `scroll` action can be confusing sometimes as it's opposite to swipe, for example, to view content at the bottom, the `scroll` direction should be set to "down". It has been observed that you have difficulties in choosing the correct direction, so if one does not work, try the opposite as well.
Text Related Operations
- Normally to select some text on the screen: <i> Enter text selection mode by long pressing the area where the text is, then some of the words near the long press point will be selected (highlighted with two pointers indicating the range) and usually a text selection bar will also appear with options like `copy`, `paste`, `select all`, etc. <ii> Select the exact text you need. Usually the text selected from the previous step is NOT the one you want, you need to adjust the range by dragging the two pointers. If you want to select all text in the text field, simply click the `select all` button in the bar.
- At this point, you don't have the ability to drag something around the screen, so in general you can not select arbitrary text.
- To delete some text: the most traditional way is to place the cursor at the right place and use the backspace button in the keyboard to delete the characters one by one (can long press the backspace to accelerate if there are many to delete). Another approach is to first select the text you want to delete, then click the backspace button in the keyboard.
- To copy some text: first select the exact text you want to copy, which usually also brings up the text selection bar, then click the `copy` button in bar.
- To paste text into a text box, first long press the text box, then usually the text selection bar will appear with a `paste` button in it.
- When typing into a text field, sometimes an auto-complete dropdown list will appear. This usually indicating this is a enum field and you should try to select the best match by clicking the corresponding one in the list.
